newsitem.title: SPAIN: Unisource not interested in Retevision bid - press.
newsitem.headline: Unisource not interested in Retevision bid - press.

text.p: European telecoms consortium Unisource has lost interest in bidding for Spain's second basic telephony operator Retevision, according to Telia director Bertil Thorngen, as reported by Spanish newspapers on Tuesday.
Sweden's Telia forms part of Unisource with Holland's KPN, Swiss Telecom and Telefonica de Espana, and the consortium had its bid for Retevision rejected in April after applying too late.
This meant that Unisource was not allowed to bid for the 60 percent sale of the telecoms firm on its own, although it could have formed an alliance with one of the other three consortiums interested.

Those consortia are firstly, AT&T and Germany's Mannesman AG, secondly Italy's Stet and Spanish electricity firms Endesa and Union Fenosa, and thirdly a group comprised of Banco Central Hispano, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom y Sprint Corporation.
These groups have until May 12 to introduce changes to the members of the consortia.
Speaking at a conference here, Throngren also ruled out Stet's entry into Unisource in substition of Telefonica, as some press reports had indicated.
